verses.text: Hezekiah sent messages to all Israel and Judah. He also wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh, inviting them to come to the LORD's temple in Jerusalem to celebrate the Passover for the LORD, the God of Israel.
The king, his leaders, and all the people in Jerusalem had agreed to celebrate the Passover in the second month.
They could not celebrate it at the normal time, because not enough priests had made themselves holy, and the people had not gathered in Jerusalem.
The plan seemed right to the king and to all the people.

So they decided to send an announcement all through Israel, from Beersheba to Dan, telling the people to come to Jerusalem to celebrate the Passover for the LORD, the God of Israel. Many people had not celebrated it in the way the law says.

So messengers took letters from the king and his leaders all through Israel and Judah. As the king ordered, the letters said, "People of Israel, come back to the LORD, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, so he will come back to those of you who escaped from the kings of Assyria.
Do not be like your ancestors and your relatives, who were unfaithful to the LORD, the God of their ancestors. He let them be destroyed, as you can see.
Do not be stubborn like your ancestors were. Give yourselves to the LORD. Come to his temple, which he has made holy forever. Serve the LORD your God, so his fierce anger will turn away from you.

If you come back to the LORD, the people who captured your relatives and children will show them mercy, and they will come back to this land. The LORD your God is kind and merciful. He will not turn his face away from you if you come back to him."
The messengers went from town to town through Ephraim and Manasseh, as far as Zebulun, but people laughed at them and made fun of them.
But some men from Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem.
In Judah also, God's power made the people agree to obey what the king and leaders had ordered, following the LORD's word.
A very large crowd of people gathered in Jerusalem in the second month to celebrate the Festival of Bread Without Yeast.
They removed the altars in Jerusalem. They also took away all the incense altars and threw them into the Kidron Valley.
They killed the Passover lambs on the fourteenth day of the second month. The priests and Levites were ashamed, so they made themselves holy and brought burnt offerings to the LORD's temple.
They took their places as the law of Moses, the man of God, required. The priests sprinkled the blood that the Levites handed to them.
Many people in the crowd had not made themselves holy. So the Levites killed the Passover lambs for everyone who was not clean, to make the lambs holy for the LORD.

Many of the people, especially from Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun, had not made themselves clean. Still they ate the Passover, which was not what the law says. But Hezekiah prayed for them: "May the good LORD forgive everyone
who sets their heart on seeking God, the LORD, the God of their ancestors, even if they are not clean by the rules of the temple."
The LORD listened to Hezekiah and healed the people.

The Israelites in Jerusalem celebrated the Festival of Bread Without Yeast for seven days with great joy. Every day the Levites and priests praised the LORD, singing with loud instruments to the LORD.

Hezekiah encouraged all the Levites who understood well how to serve the LORD. For the seven days of the festival they ate their share, offered peace offerings, and gave thanks to the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
Then all the people agreed to celebrate for seven more days. So they celebrated another seven days with joy.
Hezekiah king of Judah gave the people one thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep for offerings. The leaders gave them one thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep. Many priests made themselves holy.
All the people of Judah were full of joy, together with the priests and Levites, all the people who came from Israel, and the foreigners who came from Israel or lived in Judah.
There was great joy in Jerusalem. Nothing like this had happened in Jerusalem since the time of Solomon son of David, king of Israel.
Then the priests and Levites stood up and blessed the people. God heard them, and their prayer reached heaven, his holy home.
